Forwarding my legal notes — see inline. High-level: Orbit's withholding ask is normal for EU/APAC customers but their suggested carve (they want Redwood to assume VAT registration) is operationally risky. Recommend: accept a mutual cooperation clause + customer to provide VAT evidence; provide invoice flow that supports their local tax treatment.

Inline highlights from my review:
- Section 2.1 (Minimum Commit): the replacement clause introduces a unilateral ramp-down right tied to usage; we should tighten to require a remediation period and approval from Redwood commercial lead.
- Payment terms: Net 60 is a stretch. Suggest компромисс: Net 45 standard; Net 60 only with procurement sign-off and a credit holdback equal to 10% until payment clears.
- Taxes: propose language that customer is responsible for taxes/withholding, and Redwood will provide tax evidence on request within 5 business days.

I can take the redline and produce a clean tracked-changes doc. Ben — any commercial flexibility on holdback %? I’d like a clear fallback if they withhold.

Agree with Kim on legal posture. From a commercial standpoint, Orbit is a strategic mid-market account — we have some runway to be flexible but not to set a precedent. My proposal:
- Minimum commit: introduce a one-time ramp tolerance: if usage < 30% for two consecutive months in Q2, allow a 25% reduction in annual commit with a make-good fee equal to 15% of the reduced portion. Requires 30-day notice.
- Net terms: accept Net 60 for first invoice only (if they need it) + automated ACH and payment plan on file; otherwise Net 45.
- Taxes: customer-responsible, but we provide an invoice pack (VAT invoice + tax residency statement) and an escrow hold for disputed amounts up to 20% until resolved.

If that sounds reasonable I’ll fold into a commercial redline and send to Karthik/Kim to merge. Lauren — can you confirm accounting implication of the escrow hold?
—Ben
